📚 Today you learned

Cancel/Replace Order Risk

A cancel/replace isn't atomic — there's a gap between canceling the old order and the new one landing, and if the market moves (or you get distracted) in that gap, you're unprotected. This is exactly what happened with IQV on Aug 4: the plan was to cancel/replace a plain STOP $228 with a stop-limit 231.50/228.50, and it never happened before the trigger fired. It still worked out (only $0.09 slippage), but that was luck, not design — a bigger gap would've replayed CAPR. The GOOG order flagged above is the same failure mode one step earlier: a GTC buy sitting unconfirmed for over two weeks means if it filled, there's been no window at all to attach a stop. Treat every pending order as needing same-day reconciliation, not eventual reconciliation.

Also today: GTC (good-til-canceled) orders don't expire on their own — they sit live on the book (subject to broker time limits, often 60-90 days) until filled or manually canceled, which is exactly why a "pending" status can quietly go stale.
